_purpose: Every threshold and data-source assumption behind the Day 6 pharmacy-desert classification, so the classification is auditable without re-reading code. See DECISIONS.md (2026-07-26 entries) for the reasoning behind each choice, and LIMITATIONS.md for what this does NOT capture.

population_unit.source: Census Bureau CenPop2020 (Centers of Population), block-group level, mean center of population
population_unit.why_not_tract_centroid: A tract's geometric centroid can fall in an unpopulated part of the tract (e.g. a park, industrial zone, or empty rural land). The population-weighted centroid reflects where residents actually live within the tract.

income_threshold.definition: A tract is 'low_income' if its ACS median household income is below 80% of its county's Area Median Income (AMI).
income_threshold.source_of_80pct_rule: HUD's standard 'Low Income' definition (80% of AMI), used across federal housing/community-development programs (LIHTC, Section 8, CDBG). See https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/il.html
income_threshold.source_of_ami_figure: PROXY, not HUD's official published county AMI. HUD's bulk Income Limits dataset could not be reliably fetched this session (candidate URLs returned empty/placeholder responses, not real files). Computed instead as the population-weighted mean of median_household_income across each WA county's non-suppressed ACS tracts.
income_threshold.proxy_limitation: This proxy will differ from HUD's official county AMI, which uses a different (non-ACS-tract-average) methodology and a different income concept (family income, not household income). Treat income_status as directionally informative, not a precise HUD eligibility determination.
income_threshold.suppressed_tract_handling: Tracts with income_suppressed=true (20 of 1,784, from Day 4's audit) are marked income_status='suppressed', never defaulted to low_income or not_low_income.

urban_rural_classification.source: 2020 Census Urban Area boundaries (cartographic boundary file, 1:500,000), the delineation Census itself used to classify 2020 Census geography as urban vs. rural
urban_rural_classification.vintage_note: Deliberately NOT the older 2010 Urban Area delineation (also available, tl_2020_us_uac10.zip) - Census's own 'Urban and Rural' methodology page confirms the 2020 delineation (finalized via Federal Register notices, Mar 2022 and Dec 2022) is the correct one for 2020 Census geography.
urban_rural_classification.method: A block group is 'urban' if its CenPop population-weighted centroid falls within (ST_Within) any 2020 Urban Area polygon; otherwise 'rural'.

distance_thresholds.precedent: Matches the widely-used USDA food-desert threshold pattern (1 mile urban / 10 miles rural), adapted here for pharmacy access.
distance_thresholds.distance_type: STRAIGHT-LINE geographic distance (PostGIS geography ST_Distance), NOT road-network travel distance. Labeled explicitly as 'geographic proximity' throughout - see LIMITATIONS.md. Real travel-time/road-network distance is a documented future improvement, not implemented now.

nearest_pharmacy_search.eligible_locations: physical_locations.geom (WA) UNION border_buffer_locations.geom (OR/ID), restricted in both cases to locations with at least one associated pharmacy where included_in_access_analysis=TRUE

border_handling.method: Unioned all WA census_tracts geometries, buffered by 20 miles (geography-based), then filtered the national Census ZCTA gazetteer (2023) to OR/ID zip codes whose centroid falls within that buffer.
border_handling.pharmacy_pull_method: Same NPPES zip-sweep method as the original WA pull (Day 2), including the same LOCATION.state verification (never trust the API's state/postal_code params alone) - see DECISIONS.md 2026-07-18 WA-state-filtering entry, applied here to OR/ID.
border_handling.critical_rule: Border-buffer locations are used ONLY to compute nearest-pharmacy distance for WA block groups. They are NEVER counted as WA population, WA pharmacy inventory, or in any WA-facing count/report.
border_handling.verified_effect: Confirmed border buffer changes the outcome for real block groups, not just theoretically: e.g. Census Tract 9502, Klickitat County dropped from a WA-only 16.17mi (would exceed the 10mi rural threshold) to a true 2.37mi once the nearby Oregon pharmacy is counted. Also confirmed it does NOT over-correct: some Skamania County block groups remain correctly classified 'desert' even after the border buffer is applied, since the nearest real pharmacy (WA or OR) is still >10mi away.

final_classification_logic.is_low_access: nearest_pharmacy_miles > distance_threshold_miles (1 if urban, 10 if rural)

pharmacy_desert_status_values.indeterminate_income_suppressed: income_status == 'suppressed' - regardless of distance, since the income half of the compound definition cannot be confirmed either way

final_classification_logic.compound_definition_precedent: Mirrors the USDA food-desert model: low-income AND low-access, not either alone.
